name: New Zealand
targetIntake: Autumn 2027 (May 2027 IB session). In New Zealand this means either the July 2027 mid-year intake or, more usually, Semester 1 starting late February 2028.
tagline: One clear rule: full IB Diploma, 24 points, English and maths
summary: New Zealand has eight universities, all public, all teaching in English, and all using the same national rule for what counts as university entrance. If you hold the full IB Diploma with at least 24 points, including English as Language A (or English B at Higher Level) and any mathematics subject, you have met New Zealand University Entrance - and then each degree adds its own, higher, guaranteed-entry score. Like Australia, the academic year runs from late February to November, so a May 2027 IB session leads either to a July 2027 mid-year start or to February 2028. It is smaller, cheaper and quieter than Australia, and the post-study work visa is generous: up to three years for a bachelor's graduate.
whyConsider: The entry rule is national, published and simple: full IB Diploma, 24 points minimum, English as Language A at SL or HL (or English B at HL grade 5), plus any mathematics.

Universities publish guaranteed-entry scores per programme, so you can check your predicted score against a number rather than guess. Auckland, for example, guarantees entry to Arts and most Science programmes at 26 points and to Engineering (Honours) at 32.
Tuition sits below Australia and far below the United States for most subjects.
The Post Study Work Visa allows a bachelor's graduate to stay and work for up to three years, with no employer sponsorship needed.
Small country, small classes, and genuinely outstanding earth science, marine biology, ecology and agricultural science.
watchOuts: Hemisphere timing again. Finishing the IB in May 2027 means either squeezing into a July 2027 intake - not offered for every degree - or waiting until late February 2028.
Distance and cost of getting there. Flights to Denmark take well over a day and are expensive; going home for Christmas is a 30-hour journey into the middle of the New Zealand summer holidays.
Immigration New Zealand requires NZD 20,000 per year of living costs on top of full tuition before it grants the student visa.
The job market is small. Post-study work rights are generous but there are simply fewer graduate employers than in Australia or Canada.
Only eight universities, so if your subject is niche your choice may come down to one or two places.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: 24 points with the full IB Diploma awarded - this is the national University Entrance equivalence threshold, not an entry guarantee. Individual programmes require more.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: The University Entrance literacy requirement is met by English as Language A - literature or Language A - language and literature at Standard or Higher Level, or by English Language B at Higher Level with a minimum grade of 5. The numeracy requirement is met by any mathematics subject. Individual degrees add their own subject prerequisites and grade requirements on top.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: Universities use your total IB points out of 45 directly as a rank score. The University of Auckland states that your IB rank score equals your total IB points, and then publishes guaranteed entry thresholds against that number.
notes: Verified guaranteed-entry scores at the University of Auckland for 2027 entry: 26 points for Arts, Dance Studies, Early Childhood Studies, Education (Teaching), Fine Arts, Psychology, most Science programmes and Sport/Health/Physical Education; 27 for Commerce, Communications, Design, Urban Planning, Global Studies and Property; 28 for Biomedical Science, Health Sciences and various conjoint degrees; 31 for Nursing and Architectural Studies; 32 for Engineering (Honours); 34 for Engineering conjoint degrees.
Victoria University of Wellington states the same national rule: IB Diploma with 24 points minimum, plus any mathematics and English through Language A at SL or HL or Language B at HL.
Medicine, pharmacy and optometry are not entered directly from school. You complete a prescribed first year and then compete for entry.
Some programmes also require a portfolio, audition or interview.

portal.name: Apply directly to each university - there is no central admissions system

deadlines.label: Semester 1 2028 (main intake)
deadlines.notes: The main New Zealand intake. Applications generally open mid-year the year before. Exact 2028 teaching dates had not been published at the time of writing - check each university's academic calendar.

deadlines.label: Semester 2 2027 (mid-year intake)
deadlines.notes: The fastest route from a May 2027 IB session. Not all degrees admit mid-year - engineering, health and most professional programmes are Semester 1 only. Verify per degree.

deadlines.label: Programmes with early closing dates
deadlines.notes: Some limited-entry programmes - medicine-track health sciences, architecture, fine arts, nursing - close months before the general deadline and may require a portfolio or interview. Check the specific programme page.

deadlines.label: Fee Paying Student Visa application
deadlines.date: After you accept an offer and pay fees
deadlines.notes: You apply once you have an offer of place and evidence of funds. The visa can be granted for up to 4 years.

steps: Decide between a July 2027 mid-year start and a February 2028 start, and check whether your chosen degree has a mid-year intake at all.
Check that you will meet University Entrance: full IB Diploma, 24 points, English as Language A (or English B HL grade 5), plus any mathematics.
Compare your predicted IB total against each programme's published guaranteed-entry score.
Apply directly on the university's own international application site - there is no UCAS or UAC equivalent here. You can apply to several universities in parallel.
Submit predicted IB grades; universities will normally make a conditional offer and confirm it when your July 2027 results are released.
Accept the offer, pay the tuition deposit and arrange insurance, then apply for the Fee Paying Student Visa with proof of NZD 20,000 per year in living costs plus your tuition.
Apply for university accommodation at the same time - first-year halls are the easiest and safest option and they fill up.
application.selectionNotes: Entry is score-based against published thresholds for most degrees, with a small number of limited-entry programmes using portfolios, auditions, interviews or a competitive first-year selection. There is no personal statement culture and no national ranking system. Meeting University Entrance gets you into the university; meeting the programme score is what admits you to the degree.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: All of it. Every New Zealand university degree is taught in English.
language.englishProof: For IB students the University Entrance literacy requirement itself does the work: English as Language A - literature or language and literature at SL or HL, or English Language B at HL with a minimum grade of 5, satisfies it at the University of Auckland. Universities may still ask for IELTS or TOEFL in some cases; typical minimums are IELTS 6.0-6.5. Not verified per university.
notes: Te reo Maori is an official language and appears in university life and ceremony, but no degree requires it unless you choose it.
Immigration New Zealand may have its own English evidence requirements separate from the university's - check the visa page.

tuitionEuEea.value: Not applicable - New Zealand has no EU/EEA fee category. Danish students pay international fees.

tuitionNonEu.value: Verified example, University of Auckland: international undergraduate fees for 2026 range from NZD 40,225 for a Bachelor of Arts (excluding performance and science-based courses) up to NZD 86,561 for later years of Medicine and Surgery, for a full-time year of 120 points. Indicative 2027 figures published by Auckland run from about NZD 42,236 upwards, roughly 5% higher than 2026. All students also pay a Student Services Fee of about NZD 1,132.80 a year. Other universities are broadly similar or somewhat cheaper; individual figures were not verified for this guide.

livingCostMonthly.value: Immigration New Zealand requires NZD 20,000 for each year of tertiary study, or NZD 1,667 a month for courses shorter than a year - about NZD 1,667 a month. That is the visa minimum, not a realistic Auckland or Wellington budget.

notes: The NZD 20,000 is living costs only and sits on top of full tuition, which you must also pay or show.

The Fee Paying Student Visa costs from NZD 850. Search results also reported an International Visitor Conservation and Tourism Levy of NZD 100, which we could not confirm on the official page - check immigration.govt.nz.
The Post Study Work Visa costs from NZD 1,670 and requires you to hold at least NZD 5,000 for living expenses.
Auckland and Wellington are the expensive cities; Dunedin, Palmerston North, Hamilton and Christchurch are considerably cheaper.

funding: University international excellence scholarships. Every New Zealand university offers entrance scholarships to strong international undergraduates, usually a partial fee reduction awarded on your admission score. Amounts were not verified for this guide - check each university's scholarship page, because several have deadlines earlier than the admission deadline.
The New Zealand Excellence Awards and similar government-backed schemes target specific countries and regions; eligibility for Danish students was not verified.
Faculty awards and first-year prizes, awarded on results after you arrive.
Part-time work. Fee Paying Student Visa holders can usually work up to 25 hours a week during study and full-time in holidays, which goes further in Dunedin than in Auckland.
Danish SU may in some circumstances follow you abroad for a full degree. Check su.dk and speak to your studievejleder early.
There is no New Zealand government loan or grant for international undergraduates.
workRights: Fee Paying Student Visa holders may work part-time up to 25 hours a week while studying and full-time during scheduled holidays, depending on the conditions written on the visa; students aged 16-17 need extra permission. After graduating, the Post Study Work Visa lets a bachelor's-degree graduate (level 7 or higher) stay and work for up to 3 years, with no employer sponsorship required. You must apply no later than 3 months after your student visa expires, and hold at least NZD 5,000 for living expenses. Sources: https://www.immigration.govt.nz/visas/fee-paying-student-visa/ and https://www.immigration.govt.nz/new-zealand-visas/visas/visa/post-study-work-visa
residency: You need a Fee Paying Student Visa. You apply after you have an offer of place and have paid or arranged tuition, and you must show NZD 20,000 per year of living costs, good health and good character. The visa costs from NZD 850 and can be granted for up to 4 years, normally matching the period of study you have paid for, or until your passport expires if that is sooner. Source: https://www.immigration.govt.nz/visas/fee-paying-student-visa/
housing: First-year students are strongly encouraged into university halls of residence, and most universities guarantee a place if you apply by their deadline - take it, because private renting from Denmark is difficult and the halls are where you meet people. Otago is famous for its all-in residential first year in Dunedin. Auckland and Wellington private rents are high; Dunedin, Hamilton, Palmerston North and Christchurch are much more affordable.
healthcare: International students on a student visa are generally not entitled to publicly funded healthcare in New Zealand, so Immigration New Zealand requires acceptable medical and travel insurance for the whole period of study, and universities normally arrange or sell a compliant policy. The EHIC and the Danish yellow card are not valid. Budget for insurance as a separate annual cost.

institutions.name: University of Auckland
institutions.englishBachelors: The largest and broadest offering in the country, including conjoint (double) degrees that combine two bachelor's in about four to five years.
institutions.note: Publishes its guaranteed-entry IB scores openly - 26 for Arts and most Sciences, 28 for Biomedical Science, 32 for Engineering (Honours) - so you can tell before you apply whether your predicted score is enough.

institutions.name: University of Otago
institutions.englishBachelors: New Zealand's oldest university, with a famously residential first year and the country's strongest health sciences pathway.
institutions.note: The closest thing in the southern hemisphere to a self-contained university town - almost the whole city revolves around the campus. Medicine and dentistry are entered by competitive selection after a Health Sciences First Year, not directly from school.

institutions.name: Victoria University of Wellington - Te Herenga Waka
institutions.englishBachelors: Three-year bachelor's degrees in the capital, with strong law, public policy and creative writing.
institutions.note: States the national IB rule plainly - Diploma with 24 points minimum, any mathematics, English through Language A at SL or HL or Language B at HL - and being in the capital gives unusual access to government internships.

institutions.name: University of Canterbury
institutions.englishBachelors: Traditional campus university with the country's largest engineering school and a well-known forestry programme.
institutions.note: Two hours from the Southern Alps and the main academic gateway to Antarctic research; engineering here is the most established in New Zealand.

institutions.name: Massey University
institutions.englishBachelors: Three campuses plus the largest distance-learning operation in New Zealand; unusually strong in agriculture, veterinary science and aviation.
institutions.note: Home to New Zealand's only veterinary school and a pilot training programme that leads to a commercial licence; Palmerston North is cheap and unglamorous, which some students find perfect.

institutions.name: University of Waikato
institutions.englishBachelors: Mid-sized, with a management school and a well-regarded computing and mathematical sciences faculty.
institutions.note: Lower entry thresholds and lower living costs than Auckland, an hour and a half down the road; the machine learning group has an international reputation well beyond the university's overall ranking.

institutions.name: Auckland University of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Practice-focused degrees with compulsory work placements in many programmes; New Zealand's youngest university.
institutions.note: The applied alternative in Auckland: lower entry scores than the University of Auckland, more industry placement, and a sport science department with a genuinely strong research record.

institutions.name: Lincoln University
institutions.englishBachelors: New Zealand's smallest university, specialising entirely in land, food and environment.
institutions.note: Under 3,000 students and completely focused on land-based science - if you want agronomy, viticulture or land management this is the best fit in the country, and if you do not, it will feel very narrow.

institutions.name: Unitec Institute of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Applied bachelor's degrees in construction, computing, design and social practice, with lower entry requirements than the universities.
institutions.note: A realistic option if your IB total lands below the university thresholds but you still want a recognised New Zealand bachelor's degree and the post-study work rights that come with it - confirm the degree is at level 7 so the Post Study Work Visa applies.

institutions.name: Otago Polytechnic
institutions.englishBachelors: Hands-on bachelor's degrees in design, engineering technology, nursing and occupational therapy.
institutions.note: Small, studio-based teaching in the cheapest student city in New Zealand; a practical alternative to a research university if you want to make things rather than study theory.
